title: Evander User Manual Outline
intended_audience: operators who supervise Evander day to day
team leads who assign or review agent work
administrators who manage users, directories, policies, and integrations
support staff who investigate failed automations or approval requests

tone_guidance.technical_depth: Avoid internal implementation detail unless it helps the user make a safe operating decision.
tone_guidance.how_to_format: Each how-to should state when to use it, prerequisites, numbered steps, expected result, and common recovery paths.

sections.title: Welcome To Evander
sections.description: Introduce Evander as the operator console and automation control plane for supervised agent work. Explain what users can do with it, what it is not meant to replace, and how the system keeps human approval, auditability, and scoped access central.

subsections.title: What Evander Helps You Do
subsections.description: Describe the main user outcomes: monitor active work, create agent sessions, review approvals, manage workflows, coordinate teams, inspect audit trails, and recover from common failures.

subsections.title: Important Concepts In Plain Language
subsections.description: Define core terms such as directory, agent, session, VM, container worker, workflow, approval, tool call, artifact, add-on, and Team without exposing low-level storage or service details.

subsections.title: Operator Responsibilities
subsections.description: Explain what humans remain responsible for: approving sensitive actions, checking outputs before relying on them, maintaining user access, reviewing incidents, and keeping external systems or credentials current.

subsections.title: Safety And Trust Model
subsections.description: Summarize in user terms that Evander keeps secrets on the host, restricts agent access, records tool activity, and uses approval gates for higher-risk actions.

how_tos.title: Decide Whether Evander Is The Right Surface For A Task
how_tos.description: Walk the user through choosing between Dashboard, Agents, Issues, Workflow, Teams, and external systems based on the desired outcome.

sections.title: Getting Started
sections.description: Give first-time users a practical path from opening Evander to understanding the current system state. Keep setup wording high level and refer administrators to operational setup documents only when needed.

subsections.title: Open Evander
subsections.description: Show the usual local URL, explain sign-in behavior, and describe what a user should see after a successful login.

subsections.title: Sign In And Sign Out
subsections.description: Explain local-password and Microsoft sign-in modes from the user's point of view, including what to do when a login is rejected or a session expires.

subsections.title: Understand The Main Screen
subsections.description: Describe the header, navigation, selected directory, privilege lock, theme toggle, user menu, deployment banner, assistant launcher, and page content area.

subsections.title: Choose The Right Directory
subsections.description: Explain directories as scopes for teams, environments, tenants, or products. Describe how changing directory affects visible agents, sessions, policies, workflows, and approvals.

subsections.title: Unlock Privileged Operations
subsections.description: Explain the lock as a deliberate safety step before changes such as starting agents, deleting records, approving actions, saving configuration, or editing workflows.

how_tos.title: Open Evander For The First Time
how_tos.description: Provide steps for navigating to the Admin Web URL, signing in, confirming the active user, and checking the Dashboard for live status.

how_tos.title: Switch To A Team Or Project Directory
how_tos.description: Show how to open the directory chooser, select the desired scope, verify the current scope in the header, and avoid acting in the wrong directory.

how_tos.title: Safely Unlock And Relock Changes
how_tos.description: Explain when to unlock, how to confirm mutation buttons became available, and why to lock again after completing changes.

sections.title: Dashboard And Daily Monitoring
sections.description: Teach operators how to use the Dashboard as the first stop for answering what needs attention now.

subsections.title: Dashboard Panels
subsections.description: Describe the purpose of health, workers, agents, workflow activity, approvals, sessions, audit, reports, version, news, and capacity panels.

subsections.title: Refresh And Staleness
subsections.description: Explain when the Dashboard uses cached summaries, when to click Refresh, and when to open detail pages for a live read.

subsections.title: Attention Signals
subsections.description: Explain missing data, unavailable panels, failed workflow runs, pending approvals, unhealthy workers, high queue age, and prompt pressure in operator language.

subsections.title: Release And Product Information
subsections.description: Explain where to find version, changelog, news entries, and deployed build identity so operators know what is currently running.

how_tos.title: Run A Morning Operations Check
how_tos.description: List a daily sequence: open Dashboard, refresh, scan worker state, approvals, sessions, workflow activity, capacity, and any deployment banner.

how_tos.title: Follow A Dashboard Warning To The Detail Page
how_tos.description: Show how to use quick links from Dashboard panels to Workflow, Approvals, Sessions, Tool Calls, Configuration, Workers, or Reports.

how_tos.title: Download The Changelog
how_tos.description: Describe how to retrieve release notes from the Dashboard and use them during operator handover or incident review.

sections.title: Working With Agents
sections.description: Explain how operators create, inspect, steer, and retire agent work without requiring knowledge of the underlying execution backend.

subsections.title: Agent List And Details
subsections.description: Explain the agent list, selected agent details, labels, logs, policy, metadata, session links, VM or worker context, and current status.

subsections.title: Create An Agent
subsections.description: Describe the create flow: directory, session ID, model, target type, allowed tools, communication allowlists, bootstrap choices, and optional skills.

subsections.title: Prompt Or Resume An Agent
subsections.description: Explain direct prompts, resume thread IDs, expected responses, and how to find follow-up logs or tool calls.

subsections.title: Operator Steering

subsections.title: Lifecycle Actions
subsections.description: Describe start, stop, shutdown, destroy, revoke, and cleanup actions, including confirmation habits before destructive changes.

subsections.title: Skills For Agents
subsections.description: Explain managed skills as reusable instructions that can be selected when creating an agent or installed later.

how_tos.title: Create A Basic Agent Session
how_tos.description: Step through opening Agents, selecting a directory, unlocking, filling required fields, choosing a model/provider, selecting allowed tools, and confirming the created session.

how_tos.title: Send A Follow-Up Prompt To An Existing Agent
how_tos.description: Show how to select the agent, open the prompt action, write a clear instruction, optionally reuse the latest thread, and inspect the result.

how_tos.title: Install A Managed Skill Into A Session
how_tos.description: Explain how to pick a skill from the Skills library through the Agents tab and verify that the install action completed.

how_tos.description: Give a practical flow for reviewing the current log, sending a concise steering message, and checking whether the next output reflects the change.

how_tos.title: Retire Or Destroy An Agent Safely
how_tos.description: Explain how to confirm the agent, session, directory, work status, artifacts, and audit needs before stopping, revoking, or destroying it.

sections.title: Sessions, Access, And Policy

subsections.title: Session Expiry And Revocation

subsections.title: Allowed Tools
subsections.description: Explain how the allowed tool list controls what the session can ask Evander to do.

subsections.title: Approval Requirements
subsections.description: Explain per-session approval requirements, approval time-to-live, use counts, and strict payload matching in operator terms.

subsections.title: Allowed Scripts And Communication
subsections.description: Describe how to limit scripts, messaging targets, file receive/send permissions, file size, MIME type, extension, and metadata.

subsections.title: Scheduled Wakes
subsections.description: Explain one-time and recurring wake schedules, wake prompts, ledger entries, and retrying failed or late wakes.

how_tos.title: Require Human Approval For A Tool
how_tos.description: Show how to select the session, enable the tool if needed, require approval, adjust approval settings, save, and test that requests appear in Approvals.

how_tos.description: Explain how to locate the session, check current expiry, use the extend action, and confirm the new expiry.

how_tos.description: Explain how to create a wake schedule, choose the prompt, enable it, verify ledger entries, and retry failures.

how_tos.title: Allow A Session To Receive Or Send Files
how_tos.description: Describe how to set allowed targets, size limits, MIME types, extensions, approval expectations, and audit checks.

subsections.title: Reviewing A Request

how_tos.title: Set Up Approval Notifications
how_tos.description: Explain how to choose notify-capable communication targets and verify that approval requests reach the intended operators.

subsections.title: Tool Call Search

how_tos.description: Show how to use artifact metadata and relation links from Workflow, Team deliverables, or Tool Calls to find the producing session.
